messages:
olivia_ap: FYI vendor Reno Labs sent INV-2026-77 billed partly to Redwood Inc and partly to Redwood EU. AP noticed they charged US sales tax on the US portion and VAT on the EU portion but didn't include any W-9/W-8 or EU VAT IDs. Need docs before payment.

reno_vendor: Hi all  apologies for the messy invoice. We split the work across teams: US consulting hours (bill to Redwood Inc) + software license to Redwood GmbH. We did VAT on the license and sales tax on services. Our tax team says we should submit both W-9 (US entity) and W-8BEN-E (for our EU branch) depending on billing. Which forms do you need?

abby_tax: Short: For the US-billed portion Redwood needs either a W-9 from Reno (if Reno is US person/entity) or a W-8BEN-E if Reno is foreign. For the EU software sale billed to Redwood GmbH, VAT treatment depends on customer VAT ID and B2B reverse charge. Do we have Redwood GmbH VAT?

mike_payments: Redwood GmbH VAT: DE987654321 (we use that internally). AP: hold payment until vendor provides required tax docs and corrected invoice referencing which legal entity each line is billed to.

docbot: :no_entry: Payment placed on hold: INV-2026-77 - missing tax docs.

reno_vendor: We're registered as Reno Labs Inc (US) and also have an EU branch Reno Labs GmbH (DE). Should I upload a W-9 for the US entity and W-8BEN-E for the EU branch? Our treasurer suggests W-8BEN-E only for the EU arm.

abby_tax: If the invoice shows two separate legal suppliers (US entity for services, DE entity for license) you should provide the corresponding docs: W-9 for Reno Labs Inc lines; for DE entity, a VAT registration cert and no W-8 needed if paid in EU. If the DE branch invoices a US entity then we might need W-8BEN-E, but since it's billed to Redwood GmbH (DE) it's B2B EU and reverse charge applies.

olivia_ap: Reno - can you reissue invoice with two invoice headers (one from Reno Labs Inc -> Redwood Inc, one from Reno Labs GmbH -> Redwood GmbH) or add clear line-level supplier and VAT treatment? AP can't mix legal entities on one invoice.

reno_vendor: Yes will reissue. Q re: gross-up: our CFO says if the US payor withholds backup withholding or state sales tax they expect gross-up for the US-billed consulting portion. Is Redwood open to gross-up?

mike_payments: We don't gross-up for vendor taxes by default. If withholding is required by US federal/state law, we apply it; gross-ups require procurement/legal approval and impact P&L. Provide contract clause if previously agreed.

abby_tax: Also clarify: state sales tax is typically collected by vendor, not withheld by payer. US federal withholding on payments to vendors happens only in specific cases (e.g., backup withholding without TIN). If Reno provides a valid W-9 with EIN, no federal backup withholding.

reno_vendor: Understood. We'll upload W-9 for Reno Labs Inc (EIN 12-3456789), VAT cert for Reno Labs GmbH (UID DE111222333), and reissued split invoices with references. Expect them in ~2 hours.

docbot: :white_check_mark: Uploaded docs detected: W-9 (link), VAT cert (link). Pending validation.

olivia_ap: Thanks. AP will verify W-9 and VAT, then release US portion if no withholding. If W-9 missing or invalid we might default to backup withholding per IRS rules.

abby_tax: I'll validate W-9 quickly. If all good, we should confirm no gross-up and that vendor accepts payments net. If vendor later shows lawful withholding at foreign jurisdiction, they must provide official proof.

reno_vendor: Thanks team. We'll await payment after validation. Apologies for the invoice format - learned our billing ops need fixing. :slightly_smiling_face:
